_doc: N-197. Replayed by ../checksig-encoding-abort.test.ts through every SDK ANF interpreter in on-chain mode (TS in-process, the six drivers via --mode=on-chain) and through @bsv/sdk Spend.validate() as the oracle. Program: ../programs/checksig-or-probe.anf.json, i.e. assert(checkSig(sigA, pubA) || checkSig(sigB, pubB)). sighash = sha256("runar-n197-checksig-encoding-abort"); signatures are RFC 6979 low-S ECDSA over that 32-byte digest directly (no extra hash) plus a 0x41 sighash-type byte. sigB/pubB (priv 0x22..22) always verify, so a case that does not abort falls through to the B-arm and succeeds. Priv A = 0x11..11, the wrong key = 0x33..33. `aborts` and `reason` are the expected verdict of every SDK interpreter. For an encoding case the test re-derives that verdict from Spend on every run. A `nullfail` case (N-198) is a non-empty, well-formed signature that does not verify: a BSV node aborts there under NULLFAIL (BIP146, issue #106; ARC answers 461), but @bsv/sdk Spend has no NULLFAIL and pushes false, so for those cases Spend is NOT the oracle -- the test pins that Spend falls through to the B-arm and that every interpreter aborts as the node does.
